newsitem.title: UK: Argos first half profits set to fall.
newsitem.headline: Argos first half profits set to fall.

text.p: British retailer Argos Plc, which operates more than 400 catalogue showrooms around Britain, is expected to report lower first half profits on Monday, due to added costs and the payment of a special dividend last year.
"The company flagged the numbers up pretty well at its AGM in May, so the market will really be looking to see the pace of like-for-like sales growth," said one analyst who declined to be named.

Analysts forecast profit before tax will range from 25.5 million to 31.0 million, down from 31.8 last time. Dividend forecasts are centred on an increase to 6.0 pence per share, up from 5.3 pence previously.

There are concerns among analysts that the growth in like-for-like sales at Argos have slowed. In January, the group said its sales in the busy 35 days up to and including Christmas Eve had risen by just 4.0 percent on a like for like basis and on the whole, its second half sales were lower than it had expected.

The Bank of England's quarterly inflation report released last Wednesday showed up the strength of consumer demand on the high street fuelled by building society windfalls estimated at a total 36 billion pounds and wage growth.
But, analysts said it remains unclear how much of these windfall payments consumers are choosing to spend on the key categories for Argos of small electrical goods, toys and jewellery.
There are also worries that the catalogue format may have suffered stiffer price competition from other retailers.
In May, Argos warned on profits for the first half saying they were "unlikely to match" those in the corresponding period in 1996.
But Argos chairman Richard Lloyd told shareholders at the annual meeting that it is expecting a stronger second half performance compared with 1996.
The profits warning reflected additional costs and the adverse impact on interest income of around 3.0 million arising from the payment of last year's special dividend.
Argos said sales in the first 18 weeks of the current year were 12 percent ahead of 1996 or 5.5 percent in like-for-like terms.

Argos shares plummeted 180 pence to 598p in January, after the group reported poor sales performance over the Christmas period, but many brokers now view the stock as oversold at its current price of around 623p.
